mappings.logic: Grain is one row per order item. Sum order_items.sale_price where order_items.status is not Cancelled and not Returned. That keeps Complete, Shipped and Processing. Group by quarter of order_items.created_at and by products.department.

Same item filter as Revenue (exclude Cancelled and Returned). Gross margin $ = SUM(order_items.sale_price) - SUM(products.cost). Each item row is one unit, so cost is counted once per item. Group by quarter and department.
Gross margin $ divided by Revenue, both summed over the same kept items in the same quarter and department. Divide the sums. Do not average item-level percentages. Show nothing if revenue is zero.

Compute Revenue, Gross margin $ and Gross margin % per quarter and department. Compare each to the same quarter one year earlier. Revenue change % = (this - prior) / prior. Gross margin $ change can use the same % formula. Gross margin % change = this % minus prior %, in percentage points. 2019 quarters have no prior year, so show blank.
Calendar quarter of order_items.created_at (Q1 = Jan to Mar). Quarter boundaries are in UTC, as stored.
Join each item to its product and use products.department (Men or Women). Do not use users.gender or orders.gender. Those describe the customer, not the product department.
Filter on products.department in ('Men','Women'). Both is the default. Only these two values exist in the data.

Filter on the quarter or year derived from order_items.created_at. Suggested default: the last 4 to 8 quarters. A year-over-year comparison needs the prior-year quarter loaded too, even when it is outside the selected range.

mappings.item: Time range: quarterly 2019 to Q3 2026 (Q3 shown quarter-to-date)
mappings.logic: Include items from 2019-01-01 up to the cut-off date in Q3 2026 (July to September). Exclude any item created after 2026-09-30, because some rows run into early October 2026 (Q4). For the quarter-to-date comparison, use the same day span in Q3 2025, for example July 1 to the cut-off day.

joins: order_items.product_id = products.id (needed for department and cost)
No join to orders or users is needed. Revenue, cost, status and date are all available from order_items plus products.

gaps.item: Cost at the time of sale
gaps.reason: products.cost is one current value per product. The data has no cost history. If costs changed over time, past gross margin is restated at today's cost.
gaps.substitute: Use products.cost as-is and note this on the dashboard.

gaps.reason: There are no tax or shipping columns. sale_price is the item price, so it excludes them by construction. We cannot check that it matches the finance definition.
gaps.substitute: Use order_items.sale_price. Ask finance to confirm.

gaps.reason: The data starts on 2019-01-13. There is no 2018 data, so no 2019 quarter has a prior-year comparison.
gaps.substitute: Show YoY from Q1 2020. Q1 2019 is also a partial quarter, which makes Q1 2020 YoY look larger than the true change.

gaps.reason: Order dates in the data end on 2026-09-30, so Q3 2026 looks complete. The brief calls it quarter-to-date, but the data does not say today's date or the cut-off.
gaps.substitute: Please confirm the cut-off date. Until then, compare the same day span in Q3 2025 as the brief says.

gaps.reason: The data has no 'kept' flag. Only Complete means delivered and kept. Shipped and Processing items are not yet final, and the brief only excludes Cancelled and Returned.
gaps.substitute: Include Complete, Shipped and Processing. Optionally show Complete only as a stricter view. Needs a decision.

gaps.reason: The data has no fiscal calendar.
gaps.substitute: Use calendar quarters, as assumed in the brief.

data_notes: Use order_items.status, not orders.status. Status is recorded per item, and items in one order can differ.
Status is the current status, not the status at the time. A past quarter's revenue can fall as late returns arrive. returned_at runs to 2026-10-08, after the last order date.
Recent quarters hold more Shipped and Processing items, which may later be cancelled or returned. Recent revenue may be overstated compared with older, settled quarters, which can distort YoY.
order_items.created_at runs to 2026-10-04, but orders.created_at ends 2026-09-30. Cap the data at the Q3 cut-off so October items do not leak in.

Item dates and order dates can differ slightly. This mapping uses order_items.created_at as the order date, which avoids a join and keeps the period tied to the item. Using orders.created_at is an alternative but could move a few items across a quarter boundary.
products.department has only Men and Women. The brief's 'other departments are left out' rule does not remove anything.
Department is a product attribute. orders.gender and users.gender are customer gender, and a Women's customer can buy Men's items. Do not mix them.
Gross margin % should be a ratio of sums. Averaging item-level margins would give wrong results.
The first quarter, Q1 2019, starts on 2019-01-13, so it is a partial quarter.
Customer personal fields (names, email) are not used.
